newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Tuesday at $62.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle at $64.00, feedlot sources said.
There were light sales Monday in Kansas at $63.00, unchanged from the bulk of last week's trade. Several sources in Kansas said some packer buyers offered to call at $63.00.

"That's their way of saying they'll buy at $63.00, but they won't bid at $63.00. If I lowered my price to $63.00, they'll call in and those cattle would be sold in a heartbeat," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
Activity in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area was slow, with no sales, yet.
Feedlot sources in Kansas and the Panhandle said they expect to trade cattle Tuesday or Wednesday because of the Independence Day holiday on Friday.
"Everybody wants to get in and get it done before the holiday," a Kansas feedlot source said.
